'''Tsunaga Shrine''' (つながじんじゃ) is a {{ill|sessha|ja|擬社}} of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|內宮|lt=Kōtai Jingū (Inner Shrine)}}, part of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingū}}. Located on the west bank of the {{ill|Isuzu River|en|Isuzu River|qid=Q6089522|lt=Isuzu River}}, the shrine is situated at the foot of Mount Tsuzukayama, directly across from the {{ill|Uji Bridge (Ise City)|ja|宇治橋|lt=Uji Bridge (Ise)}}.<ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.54</ref> This article also covers {{ill|Nīkawa Shrine|ja|新川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Niikawa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11502105}} and {{ill|Ishii Shrine|ja|石井神社}}, both massha of the Inner Shrine and located at the same site.

All three shrines were designated by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with water deities as their enshrined deities.<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic">Ise Culture Institute (2008): p.116</ref>

== Overview ==
The shrines are located approximately 200 meters from the Uji Bridge, which marks the entrance to the Inner Shrine’s sacred precincts, in {{ill|Ise, Mie|ar|إيسه|azb|ایسه، میه|bcl|Ise, Mie|be|Ісэ (горад)|ca|Ise (ciutat japonesa)|ce|Исе (гӀала)|ckb|ئیسێ|cs|Ise (Mie)|de|Ise (Mie)|eo|Ise (urbo)|es|Ise (Mie)|et|Ise (Jaapan)|eu|Ise (Mie)|fa|ایسه، میه|fi|Ise (kaupunki)|fr|Ise (Mie)|gl|Ise|hr|Ise|hy|Իսե (քաղաք)|id|Ise, Mie|it|Ise (Giappone)|ja|伊勢市|ka|ისე|ko|이세시|lt|Isė (Japonija)|mg|Ise|mzn|ایسه، میه|nl|Ise (Mie)|no|Ise (Mie)|pl|Ise (Japonia)|pt|Ise (Japão)|ro|Ise, Japonia|ru|Исе (город)|sh|Ise|simple|Ise, Mie|sr|Исе|sv|Ise, Japan|szl|Ise (Japůńijo)|tg|Исе|tl|Ise, Mie|tr|Ise (şehir)|tt|Исе (шәһәр)|uk|Ісе (Міє)|ur|ایسے، میہ|uz|Ise (Mie)|vi|Ise, Mie|war|Ise, Mie|zh|伊勢市|zh_classical|伊勢市|zh_min_nan|Ise-chhī|zh_yue|伊勢|qid=Q328067|lt=Ise City}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}, Uji Imazai-cho.<ref name="ic1">Ise Culture Institute (2008): p.111</ref> Within 20 meters of Tsunaga Shrine is the {{ill|Aedo Hashihime Shrine|ja|飼土橋姫神社}}, and 50 meters away are the {{ill|Ōmizu Shrine|ja|大水神社|lt=Ōmizujinja}}, {{ill|Ōmizu Shrine|ja|川相神社|lt=Kawai Shrine}}, and {{ill|Ōmizu Shrine|ja|熊溓神社|lt=Kumabuchi Shrine}}, making a total of seven shrines in the area.<ref>Ise Culture Institute (2008): pp.111, 116</ref> The site also houses the predecessor to the Jingu Library, the old Hayasaki Library.<ref>Ise Culture Institute (2008): p.117</ref>

The three shrines share a single building constructed in {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|es|Shinmeizukuri|fr|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|ru|Симмэй-дзукури|tr|Shinmei-zukuri|zh|神明造|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}}, with wooden planks for roofing. The structure faces southwest and is surrounded by a single fence of {{ill|tamagaki|ja|玉柵}}.<ref name="sk1">Shikinaisha Research Group (1990): p.251</ref> There is no offertory box at the site. The total area of the shrine grounds is approximately 1,256 square meters (379.94 tsubo).<ref name="sk1">Shikinaisha Research Group (1990): p.251</ref> Records from 1933 mention a wisteria tree previously located at the shrine’s entrance, believed to bestow strength to children, but the tree was already gone by that time.<ref name="sk9">Shikinaisha Research Group (1990): p.249</ref>

== Tsunaga Shrine ==
Tsunaga Shrine is Ranked 14th among the 27 sessha of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office (1929): pp.9-10</ref> The area was historically called "Tsunagahara" and served as a dock for boats navigating the Isuzu River.<ref name="ic"/> It is said that Yamato-hime no Mikoto also landed here.<ref name="ic"/> The shrine is referred to as "Tsunaga Ōmizujinja" in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}.<ref>Shikinaisha Research Group (1990): p.246</ref>

The enshrined deity is Sunaga-hime no Mikoto, a water deity.<ref name="ic"/> She is said to be a child of {{ill|Ōminakami no Mikoto|ja|大水上命}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sengukan.jp/wp-content/themes/sengukan/shrine/area08/04.html?iframe=true&width=1000&height=700|title=Tsunaga Shrine つながじんじゃ>> - 125 Shrines|publisher=Jingu Office|accessdate=2013-10-01}}</ref>

== Niikawa Shrine ==
Niikawa Shrine is Ranked 6th among the 16 massha of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="uy3">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p.13</ref>

The enshrined deity is Niikawa-hime no Mikoto, a water deity.<ref name="ic"/> She was the guardian deity of a nearby dock.<ref name="gk"/> Like the other two shrines, she is said to be a child of Ōminakami no Mikoto.<ref name="gk"/>

== Iwai Shrine ==
Iwai Shrine is Ranked 7th among the 16 massha of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="uy3"/>

The enshrined deity is Takaminakami no Mikoto, the guardian deity of stone springs.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> Like the other two shrines, he is said to be a child of Ōminakami no Mikoto.<ref name="gk"/> He is also worshipped at the {{ill|Otsuchi Mioya Shrine|ja|宇治之奴鬼神社|lt=Uji-no-Nuki Shrine}}, another massha of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ise Culture Institute (2008): p.116</ref>

== History ==
Tsunaga Shrine is believed to have been founded in the 26th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}, according to the ''Yamato-hime no Mikoto Seiki''.<ref name="sk9"/> The ''Kōtai Jingū Ritual Record'' indicates that the shrine grounds once covered three chō (approximately 3 hectares), significantly larger than the present site.<ref name="sk1"/> Originally situated closer to the Isuzu River, the shrine played a more prominent role in ancient rituals.<ref name="sk9"/>

After the medieval period, rituals ceased but were revived on {{ill|December 21|ja|十二月二十一日}}, Kanbun 3 (1664), under the guidance of Ōnakatomi no Seichō, who followed the description in the ''Yamato-hime no Mikoto Seiki'' to identify the site.<ref>Shikinaisha Research Group (1990): p.247</ref> In 1871, Niikawa Shrine and Iwai Shrine were relocated to the same grounds as Tsunaga Shrine due to interruptions in their rituals.<ref name="sk9"/>

The shrine building was reconstructed in 1916 and 1956, with major renovations carried out in 1977.<ref name="sk1"/>

== Festivals ==
The shrine hosts regular festivals, including the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}} (February), {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|ja|神周祭|lt=Kannamesai}} (October), and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|ja|新周祭|lt=Niinamesai}} (November). Ceremonies for the New Year (January 1), Kigensetsu (February 11), and other events are performed remotely.<ref name="sk0"/>

== Flora ==
A 1977 survey of the grounds found 95 trees, including Kaya, Maki, Sugi, Kashi, Shii, Yabutsubaki, Inubiwa, and Akamegashiwa. Notable specimens include four camphor trees over 80 cm in diameter, with the largest measuring over 150 cm.<ref name="sk1"/>

== Access ==
; To Uji Bridge
* From {{ill|Japan Railways Group|en|Japan Railways Group|qid=Q864495|lt=JR}} {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangu Line}} or {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Kintetsu Yamada Line}}, alight at {{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise Station}} and take a Mie Kotsu Bus to "Naiku-mae," approximately 15 minutes.<ref name="mkr">Mie Prefecture Tourism Federation</ref>
* By car, 5 minutes south from either the Ise West IC or Ise IC.
; From Uji Bridge
* Cross the Uji Bridge rotary and walk approximately 200 meters (4 minutes).<ref name="ic1"/>
